messages:
katie: Customer (acme-inc) opened an escalation — seeing 504s on hosted API during morning ramp when they start long-running streaming generations. They say ~3% requests 504 over a 6m window, started ~06:12 UTC. attaching initial repro steps and curl output.

sam: can you paste the curl + response headers and any trace ids?

katie: repro loop they used: `for i in {1..50}; do curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED\" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream -d @payload.json; done`
Response snippet:
```
* Connection established
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
< server: envoy
< x-request-id: 1a2b3c4d
< date: Tue, 14 Mar 2025 06:15:03 GMT
```
Trace ids: `1a2b3c4d`, `1a2b3c4e`, `1a2b3c5f`

alex: I pulled edge logs for those ids — envoy shows `upstream_rq_timeout` and `upstream_reset_before_response_started` around the same time. Upstream (modelpool) didn't return within route timeout (30s).

lee: any signs of auth or billing rejection? looks like upstream timeouts rather than 401/402.

katie: customer said no token errors. it's only during their morning ramp (higher concurrent streaming sessions).

sam: possible suspects — keepalive/conn pool exhaustion at edge, or model server cold-starts on dedicated nodes (model load time). Also tenant-level rate cap could cause queuing and timeouts.

eng-bot: alert: tenant conn_count 540 (limit 600), edge keepalive_pool_free 6/8, h2_streams_active 420 — saturation warning at 06:10:45 UTC.

oncall: evicted a few idle conns at 06:11:00 to free pool — but traffic kept rising.

alex: putting hypothesis: customer ramps concurrent streaming requests; when their model backend scales (or spins up), initial requests wait >30s and envoy times out -> 504. Could be combined with connection pooling causing queued requests to wait behind slow model load.

katie: customer provided a model server log showing a cold load taking ~22-28s to load weights, plus an extra ~5s for adapter init. So borderline.

sam: that matches. two mitigations: 1) increase route timeout for streaming endpoints (temporarily to 60s) so in-flight cold-starts won't 504, 2) add a warmup probe on model startup so first user requests hit warmed instances, 3) throttle ingress to smooth ramp or bump reserved capacity for this tenant.

lee: we can patch a tenant-specific routing override to 60s for a quick mitigation (config change at edge routing layer). I'll schedule a short config rollout (no deploy) — need OK from oncall.

oncall: ok to rollout a short TTL config change to increase timeout for tenant `tenant-acme` from 30s -> 60s for the streaming route. Doing now, will monitor.

eng-bot: config-rollout started: rollout_id=rr-20250314-06-12, target=tenant-acme, param=timeout:60s

katie: customer testing now (they're replaying).

~2m later~

katie: customer reports failures dropped to <0.1% during same traffic pattern. Looks improved. Thanks.

sam: follow-ups: file a change to add warmup probe to our model onboarding checklist; engineering ticket to add tenant warmup autoscaler hints so modelpool can prefetch weights for known ramp patterns; also add a short-term FAQ for customers about expected cold-start window.

lee: created infra ticket INF-3421: "model warmup probe + tenant warmup hints" and assigned to eng-ml.

alex: ticket for edge config: EDGE-1975 "tenant routing override: timeout per-route" created so we can have a safer operator workflow (audit + rollback hooks).

katie: sent customer summary + mitigation steps and asked them to monitor morning ramp for 48h.

katie: resolution notes: temporary tenant timeout increased to 60s at 06:13 UTC, observed immediate reduction in 504s; next steps tracked in INF-3421 and EDGE-1975. Closing escalation but leaving monitoring open. :white_check_mark:
